name: FUN_QRTZ_FIRED_TRIGGERS
description: This table stores status information relating to triggers that have fired and the relevant execution information about the related job.

columns.name: SCHED_NAME
columns.description: Name for the given quartz schedule.

columns.name: SCHED_TIME
columns.description: Schedule time for next triggers to fire.

columns.name: ENTRY_ID
columns.description: Auto generated unique identifier.

columns.name: TRIGGER_NAME
columns.description: Functional name of the quartz trigger.

columns.name: TRIGGER_GROUP
columns.description: Group associated with quartz trigger.

columns.name: IS_VOLATILE
columns.description: Denotes persistence of jobs between program shutdown.

columns.name: IS_NONCONCURRENT
columns.description:
Stores concurrency of the job. If non-concurrent then one job will run at a time. Used for cluster coordination purposes and
clearing up blocked states.

columns.name: INSTANCE_NAME
columns.description: Holds the instance type (CLUSTERED / NON_CLUSTERED).

columns.name: FIRED_TIME
columns.description: Last execution time of the trigger.

columns.name: PRIORITY
columns.description: Priority associated with a job trigger.

columns.name: STATE
columns.description: Stores the state of the trigger.

columns.name: JOB_NAME
columns.description: Functional name of the quartz job.

columns.name: JOB_GROUP
columns.description: Group associated with quartz job.

columns.name: IS_STATEFUL
columns.description: Stores statefulness of the job. If stateful then one job will run at a time.

columns.name: REQUESTS_RECOVERY
columns.description: Instructs the Scheduler whether or not the Job should be re-executed if a 'recovery' or 'fail-over' situation is encountered. Fail-over occurs when one of the nodes fails while in the midst of executing one or more jobs.  A recovery situation is every situation that produce an 'Hard-shutdown'.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.
